items.summary: The Delhi High Court on Friday banned any victory processions after the declaration of the Delhi University Students' Union (DUSU) election results. A Division Bench of Chief Justice Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya and Justice Tejas Karia said that no procession must be carried out by the candidates, their supporters, students or anyone else, either on the roads or inside the colleges and hostels. "It will be the responsibility of the Delhi Police to ensure that any such victory procession does not take place. Any violation shall not only attract criminal and administrative action against the students but shall also amount to contempt of court," the Bench ordered. Noting that there was violation of its previous orders and the Lyngdoh Committee recommendations during campaigning, the Court said that it will impose exemplary costs on all the major student organisations. It issued notice to all the 140 candidates contesting the DUSU elections and the prominent student organisations, directing them to explain why they should not be saddled with damages "Let notice to student organisations be issued. items.title: A global guide to birthdays that nearly need a ministry of their own
items.summary: For most 76-year-olds, a birthday means cake, a call from the grandchildren and perhaps a gentle argument about sugar. For Prime Minister Narendra Modi, it now means a month-long national exercise in seva . The BJP’s Seva Sankalp Abhiyan marks 25 years since Modi first took public office as Gujarat chief minister. Ministries and state governments have been roped in, more than 500 locations are expected to participate, and the programme comes with 14 separate “modules” covering everything from health camps and cleanliness drives to overseas mahayagyas . Delhi has tied the celebrations to development projects worth around Rs 13,820 crore; Haryana has handed each deputy commissioner Rs 10 lakh for the campaign. There are diyas by the lakh, including a 5,000-diya portrait of Modi in Assam and 76,000 lamps at a midnight Ahmedabad event. This is not particularly new. Heads of states have been finding creative ways to turn their birthdays into public spectacle across history. Ancient kings commissioned monuments and rituals. items.title: Operation Toofan: Kerala police struggle to deal with addicts
items.summary: Kerala’s anti-narcotics campaign ‘Operation Toofan’, completed 100 days on September 9. The numbers are staggering: After the start of the campaign, till September 17, police have arrested 11,776 people in 10,918 cases. They also seized 23925.120 grams of MDMA and nearly 1457 kg of cannabis. But inside Kerala’s prisons and police stations, officers are confronting a different side of the drug problem: people exhibiting severe withdrawal symptoms, becoming violent in police stations and prisons, sometimes injuring themselves or others, and returning to drug use soon after they are released. One reason for this, according to investigators and mental health professionals, is the absence of protocols to identify what they have consumed or address their addiction when people are arrested with small quantities. Is Kerala’s war on drugs holistic? Aalam* was shaking and struggling to control himself while in police custody after being picked up during an Operation Toofan search. The Court called for a joint consultation among various stakeholders to draft a comprehensive set of regulations for women in the legal profession, while examining the existing gender sensitisation rules. Justice bv nagarathna and Justice augustine george masih The Court made the observations while hearing a plea seeking statutory protections for women advocates.
